structured_output.analysis: There is only one measured grid so far: iso_3.15, with KL=0.43614 (E514ab09c524e) at 3.148 avg bits. The predicted single-layer sum was 0.3983, so layer interactions add about 0.038 KL. Most of the loss sits in MLP layers quantized to int2 or int3. Examples are 27.up gptq_int3 (E04d8aa7bded), 14.down rht_gptq_int2 at 0.00633 (E4c3f9b73e065) and 3.up rht_gptq_int3 (E6f4f7ea296d5). In these layers, switching between the GPTQ and RHT variants at the same bit width is already the better choice per the table, for example for 27.up (Ef04d8aa7bded vs E8972491007e7) and 27.gate (Efa0bb391da67 vs E9eeb9841ba46). The real fix is more bits for these layers, which has to be paid for with downgrades. But I can't confidently work out a bit-neutral funding source from the budget string or from the per-layer method assignments, which aren't listed. So this round I only change options that don't alter stored bits. Turning on GPTQ act_order should cut error on layers with heavy-tailed activations, such as an activation kurtosis of 1090 at 27.up (E24beed188b6a). I also try higher damping for stability, and both together.

proposals.name: iso_3.15_actorder
proposals.rationale: Starts from iso_3.15 (KL 0.43614, E514ab09c524e). Turns on weight_algo.act_order=true for every GPTQ-family method, which leaves stored bits unchanged. The largest losses are in GPTQ int2/int3 MLP layers with heavy-tailed activations, for example 27.up gptq_int3 at 0.0057182 (Ef04d8aa7bded) with activation kurtosis 1090.09 (E24beed188b6a).

proposals.name: iso_3.15_damp05
proposals.rationale: Starts from iso_3.15 (KL 0.43614, E514ab09c524e). Raises damping from the default 0.01 to weight_algo.damp=0.05 for the low-bit GPTQ methods, without changing bits. The loss is concentrated in rht_gptq_int2 layers, for example 14.down at 0.00633466 (E4c3f9b73e065).

proposals.name: iso_3.15_actorder_damp05
proposals.rationale: Starts from iso_3.15 (KL 0.43614, E514ab09c524e). Combines weight_algo.act_order=true with weight_algo.damp=0.05 for the low-bit methods; stored bits stay the same. It targets the int2/int3 MLP losses, for example 3.up rht_gptq_int3 at 0.0064177 (E6f4f7ea296d5) and 14.down rht_gptq_int2 at 0.00633466 (E4c3f9b73e065).
